encoding.rationale: os.path.exists(restoreLogPath) is an opaque filesystem probe. The path string itself is a free public input (--restore-from-log, type=str, resolved via os.path.abspath + process CWD), but its truth value under exists() is determined entirely by live filesystem state, not by any cli/yaml/int/bool input. The only sound encoding is to lift the exists() result to a free Boolean and reason about the surrounding Not.
encoding.note: z3 trivially proves the abstraction is satisfiable in both polarities (a 1-var formula). This shows both branches are reachable in principle; it does NOT prove reachability from public inputs, because the oracle is unconstrained by them.

true_examples.method: by-value (real os.path.exists on absent path) + z3 abstraction sat
true_examples.behavior: guard args.RestoreLog truthy -> path resolved -> exists() False -> branch taken -> printExit('restore log file: ... is not existing, abort. Please check')

false_examples.method: by-value (real os.path.exists on a file we created) + z3 abstraction sat
false_examples.behavior: guard args.RestoreLog truthy -> path resolved -> exists() True -> branch skipped -> falls through to restore_prob_sol_map(restoreLogPath)

crosshair.reason: The extractable helper's entire body is the os.path.exists() I/O oracle; CrossHair cannot symbolically explore the filesystem, so it would either treat exists() opaquely (no meaningful path split) or report 'no counterexample found' against any contract. Per task note: absence of counterexample != proof. Running it would produce a vacuous result, so it is intentionally not run. The branch is pinned by-value with real filesystem state instead.

notes: Branch predicate is a single filesystem existence probe. The path STRING is a public input (CLI --restore-from-log -> os.path.abspath -> Path), but the branch outcome depends on whether that path names an existing entry on the live filesystem at runtime -> runtime-dependent, solver_status=unknown. z3 confirms both polarities of the lifted boolean are satisfiable (both branches structurally reachable) and real os.path.exists() calls ground concrete TRUE/FALSE witnesses. The surrounding guard (line 534: if args.RestoreLog) only requires a truthy string, which both witness paths satisfy. To pin behavior in a reified test: pass an absent absolute path -> expect SystemExit/printExit (TRUE branch); pass a path to a file you create in a tmp dir -> branch skipped, proceeds to restore_prob_sol_map (FALSE branch).
